question: Can the current RIC LM Studio provider path be assumed to load or hotswap a separate LoRA adapter at inference time?

findings.finding: LM Studio native v1 REST documentation exposes chat plus model list/load/unload/download endpoints and load-time model configuration, but the current documented model-load and chat interfaces inspected do not expose a LoRA/adapter parameter.
The lmstudio-ai/lms issue requesting inference-time LoRA adapter support remains open in the web state inspected on 2026-08-21.
The corresponding lmstudio-ai/mlx-engine LoRA support request also remains open in the web state inspected on 2026-08-21.

A historical LM Studio bug report describes a Qwen3 fine-tune produced by merging Axolotl-trained LoRA adapters into the base and then converting/quantizing the merged result to GGUF. This demonstrates a merged-model workflow can be brought to LM Studio, but it is user-reported evidence and not an official native adapter lifecycle contract.

ric_consequences: Do not design the future RIC adapter lifecycle on the assumption that LM Studio can activate, disable or hotswap PEFT LoRA adapters in place.
PEFT hotswap capability and LM Studio serving capability are separate technical questions.
The behavioral LoRA experiment can still train and evaluate adapters outside LM Studio before any runtime integration decision.
The runtime integration gate after P3.5 must freshly recheck LM Studio capability because upstream support can change.

If LM Studio still lacks native adapter support at integration time, possible technical families include serving through another adapter-aware backend or creating a derived merged model artifact for LM Studio. These are options for Codex audit, not R&D architecture prescriptions.
A merged derived model would weaken the operational convenience of adapter hotswap and would require explicit provenance tying the derived artifact to base model plus adapter version.
Changing inference backend solely to gain hotswap is not automatically justified; compare maintenance, AMD support, API compatibility, observability and rollback.
falsification_or_refresh: Before any runtime WO, search current official LM Studio documentation for an explicit adapter/LoRA load or inference parameter.
If official support exists later, replace this audit with a fresh capability proof and test the exact API locally.
Do not infer feature absence solely from old open issues; the current official docs and a local capability test take precedence.
